column2: req_desc

Intake layouts
The intake workspace takes the published phone, tablet and desktop arrangements, with the "Create specimen" review as a bottom sheet on phones and every target at least the configured minimum, as qualified in Screens and layout.

Intake photo slotting and confirmation
The dealer places each staged face photograph into its slot by touch drag, tap-then-tap or keyboard, enters the specimen reference and creates the specimen only by confirming the "Create specimen" review, as qualified in Interactions.

Intake storage, refusals and duplicates
Creating a specimen stays pending until MinIO confirms both photographs, refuses each wrong-type, SVG, oversized or out-of-range file in its slot before anything is stored, and lets exactly one of two drafts claim a reference while the loser keeps both staged faces, as qualified in Business rules.

Coin photograph presentation
At its lowest zoom on a phone, the attribution viewer shows the specimen's coin photograph as a complete coin with its whole rim and readable relief.

Attribution layouts
The attribution workspace keeps the mintmark viewer above the note on phones, beside it on tablets and inside the inspector beside the stock grid on desktops, with the "Quarantine attribution" review reachable in each.

Mintmark zoom and quarantine input
The dealer zooms the mintmark by pinch or the published keys while the touched image point stays put, types an attribution note and confirms quarantine through its review, working the same under reduced motion.

Quarantine feedback and conflicts
Confirmed quarantine is announced pending then saved, makes the specimen ineligible for album holes and offers, and a save over a newer attribution is refused with the conflict notice while the unsaved note stays, as qualified in Business rules.

Mintmark legibility
At every zoom step the mintmark evidence stays sharp enough to read the letter and its punch details, with the note beside or below it.

Reconciliation layouts
The reconciliation workspace stacks register reference and specimen photograph on phones, pairs them on tablets and keeps both inside the desktop inspector.

Reference wipe and correction input
The dealer compares register reference and photograph with the Slate rule wipe by drag or keys, types a catalogue reference correction, retries the register and saves through the "Save reconciliation" review.

Register outages and session resume
Rate-limited, timed-out, malformed and missing register replies keep reconciliation visibly pending with the server-stated countdown or a retry, never lose the correction or divider position, and a session that ends mid-correction resumes the same save exactly once after signing in again, as qualified in Business rules.

Reference alignment
Register reference and specimen photograph line up across the wipe divider so the same mintmark and rim sit in the same place, without crops that hide either.

Tray layouts
The tray keeps its row-major cell orientation and holder proportions on phones, tablets and desktops, with paired tray and holder panes on tablets.

Holder placement input
The dealer moves a holder into a tray cell by touch drag, tap-then-tap or keyboard pickup and confirms it through the "Place holder" review, and a cancelled placement leaves occupancy unchanged.

Placement refusals and contention
A holder too large for a cell or a drop into an occupied cell is refused with its own notice, and when two screens claim one cell exactly one wins while the other keeps its unplaced holder, as qualified in Business rules.

Holder fit drawing
Holders and cells are drawn to scale so a slab visibly overhangs a cell that a flip fits inside.

Album layouts and targets
The album renders whole in a phone column, beside its candidates on tablets and in the inspector on desktops, with every hole, chip and confirm control at least the configured target size and no sideways scrolling.

Album hole filling input
The dealer fills a hole by touch drag, tap-then-tap or keyboard and the "Fill album hole" review, and cancelling leaves the gap open.

Album exclusions and live gaps
Album holes come only from stored register records, quarantined and reserved or outbound specimens are refused with their own notices, an accepted fill updates another open screen without reload, and holes reopen when a filling specimen becomes ineligible, as qualified in Business rules.

Album gap presentation
Open holes read as named missing issues with their mintmark, not as blank or collapsed space.

Condition layouts and marker registration
The condition workspace takes the published arrangements, and a placed marker stays within the configured tolerance of its scratch across viewport changes, zoom and divider positions.

Condition wipe and marker input
The dealer moves the Slate rule wipe and places the condition marker by drag, keys or the image coordinate fields, writes a condition note and saves it through its review, the same under reduced motion.

Condition save conflicts and image retry
A saved condition note is announced pending then saved in original-image coordinates, a stale second save is refused while keeping its note and coordinates, and a failed photograph load shows a retry that restores the image with its markers, as qualified in Feedback states.

Registered condition markers
The condition marker sits visibly on the same scratch in both photographs.

Keeper list layouts
The keeper preference list takes the published arrangements, including its review.

Keeper reorder input and undo
The dealer reorders keepers by touch or keyboard pickup, confirms the order through its review, and undoes the last confirmed move through the same review.

Keeper order announcements and contention
Each staged move, pending save, saved order and restoration is announced, another open screen shows the saved order without reload, and when two screens save at once the loser re-renders in the server's order with the conflict notice.

Keeper comparison scale
Keeper chips show the specimens at one image scale so their different wear can be compared.

Offer layouts
Offer assembly stacks the two baskets with a review bottom sheet on phones, pairs them on tablets and shows the exchange list beside the basket inspector on desktops.

Basket assembly input
The dealer moves their duplicates and the counterpart's specimens into the matching baskets by touch drag, tap-then-tap or keyboard and sends through the "Send reciprocal offer" review.

Offer reservation and step-up send
Sending reserves both baskets together only for register-reconciled specimens and only with a fresh step-up, a specimen already reserved elsewhere leaves both baskets unchanged, and the counterpart's open screen shows the sent offer without reload, as qualified in Business rules.

Basket distinction
The dealer's basket and the counterpart's basket remain unmistakably separate, including in the narrow review sheet.

Counteroffer layouts
The counteroffer workspace keeps both offer sides, the current version and the response window readable on phones, tablets and desktops, with its reviews reachable.

Replacement and step-up acceptance input
Either party replaces an offered specimen by touch or keyboard through "Replace offered specimen", and accepts the current version only after completing the real Keycloak one-time-code challenge from "Accept offer version".

Voided acceptance, holds and windows
A replacement clears both acceptances on both open screens without reload, a counterpart's staged replacement holds that duplicate until their screen has been gone past the grace period, and both parties see the server's remaining response time and expiry rather than their device clock, as qualified in Business rules.

Replacement imagery
The replaced specimen's image changes in its own slot while the rest of both baskets stays still.

Dispatch layouts
The dispatch workspace shows a phone sleeve sequence, tablet manifest and evidence panes and the desktop list with inspector, and its closed review sheet takes no focus or taps.

Manifest reorder and freeze input
The dealer reorders the packing manifest by touch or keyboard pickup with each item's photographs attached and freezes it only by confirming "Freeze dispatch evidence".

Freeze feedback and frozen conflicts
Freezing stays pending until MinIO confirms every immutable evidence object, and any later reorder or freeze is refused with the frozen notice while the frozen order stays, as qualified in Business rules.

Sleeve sequence presentation
The pictured sequence reads in the same order as the physical packing sleeves.

Receipt layouts
The receipt workspace stacks arrival and dispatch photographs on phones, shows them side by side on tablets and keeps the comparison in the desktop inspector.

Arrival zoom and receipt input
The receiving party zooms the arrival photograph by pinch or keys, ticks "Manifest matches" and records receipt through its review with a fresh step-up.

Receipt transfer and ended sessions
A first receipt waits for the counterpart, matching receipts from both parties swap ownership in one step and announce it on both screens, an open dispute holds the transfer, and a counterpart whose password changes loses the screen and records nothing, as qualified in Business rules.

Receipt comparison fairness
Dispatch and arrival photographs are shown at matching scale and orientation so the same condition feature can be judged.

Dispute layouts
Dispute evidence stays full width with reachable notes on phones, pairs with its details on tablets and sits in the desktop inspector, with both dispute reviews reachable.

Damage marker and resolution input
A party places the damage marker on the arrival photograph by touch, keys or coordinates, opens the hold through its review, and the parties propose and approve a resolution with focus returning to each opener.

Dispute hold, evidence links and marker conflicts
An open dispute holds ownership transfer on both screens until both parties approve a resolution, private evidence links work only for the dispute's parties until they expire or are revoked, and when two screens move one marker the loser shows the server's position, as qualified in Business rules.

Damage marker clarity
The damage marker points at the intended physical feature without covering what is needed to judge it.

Audit layouts and stable paging
The audit tray keeps its orientation at every published viewport and after rotation, the stock list pages in capped pages that never repeat or skip a specimen while holders move between cells, and the audit list pages through each cell exactly once, as qualified in API.

Audit cell navigation and missing marks
The dealer moves between audit cells by swipe, arrow keys or the cell buttons, stopping at the ends, and records a missing item through its review, including while offline, the same under reduced motion.

Offline audit sync and live observers
Queued audit marks survive reload, replay once each in recorded order on reconnect with each step announced, update another open screen without reload, and keep a newer server change as a visible conflict, as qualified in Business rules.

Tray orientation presentation
The audit tray stays visually fixed while the selected cell and missing mark change.

Desk shell layouts and breakpoints
The desk shell shows the published masthead, tabs, corner block, directory, fact boxes and footer at each viewport, switches layout exactly at the published widths without losing the open draft or focus, and keeps closed sheets and the desk tools dialog hidden and inert.

Desk tools, sheets and session resume
The dealer opens desk tools and review sheets by touch or keyboard with trapped focus and focus return, and a confirmed action whose session ended resumes exactly once after "Sign in again".

Revocation, outages and published surface
A revoked or password-changed counterpart loses private evidence within the live bound with no later write succeeding, every unreachable dependency shows its outage copy without false success, and counterparts and strangers reach only the published routes, as qualified in Server boundary.

Desk shell look
The desk carries the grey-ground, white-sheet, slate-ruled, teal-and-bold reference-desk look with coin photographs as the only rich surface.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and its commands build and serve the app with no manual step.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, with its licence.
Shipped packages and assets use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or SIL OFL 1.1 licences.
The app stores data only in Postgres and MinIO: no other database, cache, queue or file-based store.
The provisioned service configuration is left unedited; Keycloak is configured only at run time through the app's own service account.
Saira, Archivo and Lucide icons are bundled with the app, and the browser loads nothing from third-party origins other than the Keycloak sign-in pages.
No real coin, dealer, auction archive name, wordmark or copy is used; all names, coins and register data are invented.
